verdict: Public Storage grew revenue 12% to $1.37B after closing two major acquisitions that added more than 1,100 stores, though the deals' $115M of transaction costs pulled GAAP profit down to $378M.

segments.name: Self-storage facilities
segments.note: Rent and fees from storage units — supercharged this quarter by the acquired National Storage Affiliates and Public Storage Canada stores; long-standing same-store revenue rose 0.5%.

segments.name: Ancillary operations
segments.note: Tenant reinsurance, merchandise sales, managing other owners' facilities and lending — growing fast alongside the bigger portfolio.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings over their useful lives — jumped after the acquisitions added thousands of stores to the books. Mostly a paper charge: buildings often hold their value.

opex.name: Transaction & integration
opex.note: One-time costs of buying and absorbing National Storage Affiliates and Public Storage Canada.

opex.name: Interest expense
opex.note: Interest on $12.2B of debt used to buy and build facilities.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Head office and running the company.

opex.name: Real estate acquisition & development
opex.note: Costs of evaluating and developing new facilities that are expensed rather than added to the balance sheet.

otherDetail: Interest and other income of $15M, a $27M gain on selling real estate and a $10M foreign-currency gain, partly offset by a $5M loss from unconsolidated real estate ventures — a net $46M boost (components as rounded in the release). Separately, the company recorded a $15M income-tax benefit, unusual for a REIT, which adds to profit below the tax line.
footerNote: REIT adaptation: the cost of revenue is the cost of operating the storage facilities ($333M) plus ancillary operations ($44M). Interest expense sits in running costs because Public Storage lists it among the expenses deducted to reach operating income. Net income here is the consolidated $378M; after preferred dividends and other allocations, $312M was allocable to common shareholders. FFO and Core FFO are non-GAAP measures defined by Nareit and the company, shown as KPI chips only — GAAP net income is the bottom line.
follow100Note: Depreciation is a paper charge on buildings, which is why REIT investors also watch Core FFO. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Two deals remade the map
takeaways.text: Public Storage closed its all-stock acquisition of National Storage Affiliates in July and bought Public Storage Canada for $1.2B (including assumed debt) in September, ending the quarter with 4,764 facilities and about 339M square feet. It expects $110–130M of yearly run-rate savings within three to four years.

takeaways.title: The core stores steadied
takeaways.text: Same-store revenue rose 0.5% and same-store profit (NOI) rose 0.5% as occupancy improved to 92.2% and fewer customers moved out. Management raised full-year guidance for same-store NOI and Core FFO per share.

takeaways.title: Core FFO inched up
takeaways.text: Core FFO per share (non-GAAP) rose 0.7% to $4.34 even as GAAP EPS fell 36% to $1.69. The gap is mostly the $115M of deal costs and the much larger depreciation bill on the newly bought stores — both of which FFO adds back.

oneTimers: Transaction and integration costs of $115M for the National Storage Affiliates and Public Storage Canada deals are the main reason GAAP net income fell 27% even as revenue rose 12%.
Profit also includes a $27M gain on selling real estate, a $10M foreign-currency gain and a $15M income-tax benefit — items that will not necessarily repeat.
